question: Can a small universal radial relocation of the P0554 extra gravity response improve galaxy rotation and cluster lensing together while remaining Solar-System safe?

formula.interpretation: lambda<1 compresses the extra response inward; lambda>1 expands it outward; f=0 or lambda=1 is exactly the parent

object_split.rule: SHA256(UTF-8 object name), first eight hex digits modulo 4
object_split.galaxy_rows: outer_holdout radii only; all per-galaxy nuisance values remain frozen
object_split.cluster_rows: all radii of a system remain in the same partition

selection.solar_gate: Cassini, Earth, and Mercury proxies must all pass
selection.cluster_metric: equal-system CLASH acceleration RMSE in dex
selection.primary_rank: maximize the smaller of galaxy gain and cluster gain
selection.tie_break: maximize mean of the two gains, then smaller route fraction, then lambda closest to one

evaluation.RXJ1347_geometry: archived all-six-image ordinary geometry; no geometry or gravity refit
evaluation.RXJ1347_score: exact roots for three second images after each first image fixes its source

claim_limits: The remap is a phenomenological weak-field operator, not a derived covariant field equation.
P0554 and the SPARC/CLASH data were used in earlier exploratory stages; these partitions are formula holdouts only, not pristine theory-validation samples.
CLASH accelerations and RXJ1347 target products were reconstructed under conventional lens modeling assumptions.
The radial extrapolation over a shifted endpoint uses the local log-log slope of the inferred extra-flux profile.
The Solar test is an isolated-Sun proxy and not a full ephemeris or post-Newtonian parameter fit.
A grid winner is two-parameter model selection and is not equivalent to a parameter-free prediction.
